implement: legion-worker: the phase contract — the shared workspace, the commit and push rules, the pull request body template and, through references/pr-body.md, what counts as a proof; the implementer's E2E line here is a CI run, so the rules for naming a run, its observation and its negative control are the ones that decide whether the phase is done
ce-simplify-code: the diff touches runtime Go in packages/envoy/infra, so the one simplify pass of the first implementing round applies at the proved head
dispatch-first and dispatch: any write to Dispatch (a question for the architect is Envoy, but a standalone human to-do is a dispatch ask) goes through them
test: legion-worker and its references/pr-body.md: the tester verifies the implementer's proof and adds its own; here the proof is a CI job that no pod can re-run, so the reference's rule on reading CI for everything static, and on naming a missing surface rather than passing the phase, is what governs the verdict
dispatch-first and dispatch: before filing or asking anything on Dispatch
review: legion-worker with references/review-threads.md (one disposition reply per thread, resolved by the implementer) and references/merge-gate.md (the order of a review round, the approval of a head by SHA, and what READY checks)
dispatch-first and dispatch: before any Dispatch write

findings.finding: F1: the natslive proof cannot reach the hub's own rendering (resolveListener is unexported and hard-codes port 9020 and nats://127.0.0.1:4222), so a core test could only re-spell the composed address as a literal and a wrong concatenation in gcp would still pass.
findings.answer: Decision D1 in plan.md: core gains TailnetHostName(hostname, tailnetDNSName), gcp's resolveListener calls it, the live test calls it, and task T4.4 asserts the golden's rendered value equals that function's result for the example hub. The rendered value is unchanged from the spec's.

findings.finding: F2: the spec has no Acceptance section, so nothing says what each run must show.
findings.answer: plan.md states ten acceptance criteria, A1 to A10, each with the surface and the exact command that checks it.

findings.finding: F3: gcp/construct_test.go's plainInputs() and gcp/natshub_test.go's exampleArgs() both run a listener with no tailnet name, so the new refusal reddens the whole gcp package unless both fixtures change in the same commit.
findings.answer: Tasks T4.1 and T4.2 add TailnetDnsName/tailnetDnsName to both fixtures, in the same task as the golden they move.

findings.finding: F4: the spec does not say whether the optional list of further addresses is a hub input or a listener property, and provider_test.go pins only gcp:HubListener's required set, so a new property there would be invisible to the schema test.
findings.answer: Decision D2: it is listener.allowedHosts, following the spec's wording; task T5 extends provider_test.go to pin gcp:HubListener's property set beside its required set. Named to the architect as a consumer-visible schema shape.

findings.finding: F5: envoy-infra-go is not a required check on main and its natslive step is the only place the proof ever runs, so 'CI is green' cannot be the criterion; and a vacuous pass is possible (a 503 while starting, an exempt path, a status-only assertion).
findings.answer: Criterion A7 names the job, the step and the command; task T6.3 requires requireHealthy before the assertion, a /v1 route rather than an exempt path, status 200 exactly, and a body holding ENVOY_ALLOWED_HOSTS on the refusal. The implementer records in the pull request body that this job is not required, so the reviewer and merger read it by name.

findings.finding: F6: postListener dials 127.0.0.1 and requires 200, so the harness cannot send a Host it does not dial.
findings.answer: Task T6.1 adds a request helper beside it that sets req.Host and returns the status and body, leaving postListener untouched.

findings.finding: F7: Env renders a fixed order and the golden is the instance template's user-data, so the slot is a one-way decision and the change replaces a hub's VM.
findings.answer: Decision D6 names the slot (immediately after ENVOY_LISTEN_HOST) and requires Env's doc comment to change with it; task T7.6 and T7.7 add tailnetDnsName and the listener's allowedHosts to the 'Updating a hub' list and record that the move replaces the VM of every hub that runs a listener, once, and no hub without one.

findings.finding: F8: an nkey seed lower-cased matches the listener's own host-name rule, so an entry or the tailnet name could carry one into the cloud-config and into a refusal that quotes it.
findings.answer: Decision D4 and tasks T1.3, T3.3, T2.2 and T4.6: the seed refusal comes first in core's entry check, tailnetDnsName and every listener.allowedHosts entry join seededInput, and both refusal tables gain rows.

findings.finding: F9: normalisation and duplicates are unspecified, and the golden's text depends on the answer.
findings.answer: Decision D3: entries are rendered as written, not normalised and not de-duplicated, and refused only in the cases the listener refuses one — the spec's stated contract. The listener normalises at boot and compares with slices.Contains, so neither costs anything.

findings.finding: F10: the spec settles only the missing-name case, not a tailnetDnsName set on a hub with no listener.
findings.answer: Decision D5: the shape is checked whenever the value is non-empty, beside hostnameRule in newSettings; the missing-name refusal lives in resolveListener; a listener-less hub that sets the name is not refused, because the spec says such a hub is unaffected.

findings.finding: F11: only the fully-qualified name is rendered, so a client dialling the hub by its bare MagicDNS label or its tailnet IP still gets 421, and the repository already tells clients to reach this machine by its short label for NATS.
findings.answer: The plan follows the spec (fully-qualified name rendered; anything else goes in listener.allowedHosts, which is what that input is for) and makes the limit explicit in the operator document, so the deployment follow-up checks what clients actually dial before moving the pin. Raised to the architect as an open point for the spec's owner.

findings.finding: F12: mirroring parseAllowedHosts in core leaves a drift hazard, which a test-only import of packages/envoy/internal/config closes at no release cost.
findings.answer: Task T2.3: an ordinary core test drives both parsers over one table and asserts they agree, plus an import-boundary assertion in the style of gcp/imports_test.go that go list -deps for infra/core never names internal/config. Verified that a non-test import would add that package to the plugin's release-cut set, which a test-only import does not.

findings.finding: F13: the host guard is unreleased (packages/envoy/CHANGELOG.md's entry is under Unreleased), so the operator document cannot name a release to pin.
findings.answer: Task T7.3 forbids inventing a version: the rewritten paragraph names the behaviour and the changelog and leaves the version to the deployment follow-up that moves the pin.

findings.finding: F14: the spec's measurement of 2026-10-22 and the count of 92 of 107 live sessions cannot be re-derived from the repository.
findings.answer: plan.md's closing section marks both as the architect's recorded observations, and no acceptance criterion depends on either.

findings.finding: F15: the spec's list of document changes is two sentences short (the 'Updating a hub' input list, and the claim that the YAML example's template user-data is the golden byte for byte), and no changelog, README or listener-side document needs an edit.
findings.answer: Task T7 lists seven places and ends by naming the documents checked and deliberately left alone, the changelog among them.

specDepartures.spec: The hub 'works the address out itself: gcp:NatsHub takes tailnetDnsName, and packages/envoy/infra/gcp/natshub.go renders ENVOY_ALLOWED_HOSTS=<the hub's hostname>.<tailnetDnsName> into the listener's container through core.ListenerConfig'.
specDepartures.plan: The concatenation is one exported function in core, TailnetHostName(hostname, tailnetDNSName), which gcp's resolveListener calls to fill core.ListenerConfig.AllowedHosts. The rendered value is identical; only the place the two strings are joined moves from gcp to core.
specDepartures.evidence: The behavioural proof has to run in packages/envoy/infra/core, the only package CI runs under the natslive tag (.github/workflows/envoy-and-contracts.yaml:918-919). A core test cannot reach gcp's unexported resolveListener, which hard-codes Port 9020 and nats://127.0.0.1:4222 (gcp/natshub.go:301-324) and so cannot run against a test container (core/permissions_live_test.go:258-266 needs a free port and the container's URL). With the join in gcp, the live test could only re-spell the address as a literal, and a wrong concatenation there would pass the proof and ship the 421.

specDepartures.spec: Each further address entry 'is refused while Pulumi previews it in the same cases the listener refuses one at boot, which are anything that is not a plain host name or IP address: an entry carrying a port, a scheme or a path, brackets around anything but an IPv6 address, or a wildcard'.
specDepartures.plan: Those cases, and one refusal the listener does not make: an entry holding an nkey seed is refused first, naming the entry's path and never its value.
specDepartures.evidence: An nkey seed is 58 ASCII alphanumerics, so its lower-cased form matches the listener's own dnsName rule (packages/envoy/internal/config/config.go:78-80) and would be accepted as a host name, rendered into the cloud-config and quoted by a %q refusal. The module refuses a seed where it enters, before any refusal that quotes the value (packages/envoy/infra/AGENTS.md, 'Refusals'), and gcp:Dispatch already pins exactly this for its own tailnetDnsName (gcp/dispatch_test.go:245).
